description: We are Team The Straw Hats. We enjoy what we do, and we are very interested in the topic that we chose. We are very good at front-end development, backend integrations, and also establishing a full working website based on creative ideas. We critically think, and we creatively upload.
summary: Standard Earth fire tests fail in space because flames behave completely differently without gravity. Planned lunar habitats and rovers make this risk even sharper by raising cabin oxygen to 30-34% at lower pressures (8.2-10.2 psi) so astronauts can go on spacewalks without hours of nitrogen purging. We built FLARE (https://flare-up-tau.vercel.app/) to turn decades of raw NASA microgravity fire experiments into a practical engineering workbench. FLARE combines a 6-engine physics and AI backend (trained on 29 NASA PSI investigations, 1,981 test runs, and 33,686 research excerpts) with a zero-install browser studio featuring 18 curated investigations and 1,616 flight runs. Engineers can test cabin materials across orbital, lunar, and Martian gravity, inspect 25 zoomable charts, calculate minimum safe polymer thicknesses, and size cabin fire-suppression systems in milliseconds.
details:
WHY WE BUILT FLARE

On Earth, hot air rises. Buoyancy pulls fresh oxygen into a fire from below and pushes smoke upward. In microgravity (0g) or partial gravity on the Moon (0.166g) and Mars (0.38g), that natural updraft disappears. Because of this, spacecraft fires act in counterintuitive ways:

• Gentle air vents feed the fire: In completely still air, a microgravity flame can choke on its own exhaust. But gentle cabin ventilation (0.05 to 0.20 m/s) brings in fresh oxygen faster than diffusion without blowing the flame out, causing materials that self-extinguish on Earth to burn rapidly in orbit.

• Invisible cool flames: After a visible flame goes out, low-temperature chemical reactions (550-800 K) can keep burning invisibly, producing carbon monoxide and reigniting the moment cabin fans turn back on.

• Clumped smoke vs. lunar dust: Longer residence times create long, chain-like soot particles (Df ≈ 1.65) that blind standard Earth smoke detectors and must be separated from lunar dust.

• The Artemis atmosphere problem: To avoid multi-hour pre-breathe delays before astronauts enter 4.3 psi, 100% O2 spacesuits, future lunar habitats and rovers plan to run at 8.2-10.2 psi with 30-34% O2. Standard 1g NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 screening cannot safely predict how materials burn in these environments, and NASA's Physical Science Informatics (PSI) data is spread across hundreds of separate CSVs and PDFs.

WHAT FLARE DOES

FLARE (https://flare-up-tau.vercel.app/) brings these datasets and physics models together in four connected workspaces:

1. Virtual Test Lab: Users can adjust oxygen (14-100%), pressure (4.3-60 psi), airflow (0-0.5 m/s), gravity (0g ISS, 0.166g Moon, 0.38g Mars, 1g Earth), and material thickness (0.2-10 mm). FLARE immediately calculates flame spread speed (mm/s), 95% confidence bounds, and the closest matching NASA spaceflight tests. It also runs an inverse solver across 8 spacecraft polymers (PTFE, Kapton, Ultem, PEEK, Nomex, PMMA, SIBAL) to find the minimum thickness required for a material to self-extinguish, alongside CO2 suppression mass (>50 kg for a 65 m³ lunar cabin) and a 300-second cool-flame hold timer.

2. Visual Analytics Studio (25 Techniques): Includes 2D Regime Heatmaps, 3D Manifolds, Parallel Coordinates, Ternary Diagrams, Cool-Flame Phase Planes, and Sankey Thermal Splits. Every graph includes a dedicated Zoom Lock button below the chart so scrolling the page never accidentally messes up the view, paired with Desmos-style XY/X/Y mathematical domain zooming.

3. Data Archive & Multi-Run Comparator: Lets users search and filter 18 primary NASA PSI investigations (1,616 high-fidelity flight runs), read indexed sections of the 50-page ISS Researcher's Guide to Combustion, explore 8 mission/spinoff cases, and overlay up to 4 test runs side by side.

4. Model Console: An interactive engineering assistant that answers questions using live chamber telemetry, generates clickable inline charts, and cites exact NASA PSI runs.

HOW IT WORKS & OUR DUAL-LAYER DATA PIPELINE

We built an automated crawler to gather 213 raw files (404.94 MB) from psi.nasa.gov, cleaning mixed encodings and unit mismatches.

• Backend Training Corpus: We standardized 29 NASA PSI investigations into 1,981 telemetry rows and 33,686 text chunks from 175 scientific PDFs, the ISS Researcher's Guide, and 10 NASA historical/spinoff resources.

• Curated Live Browser Archive: We packaged 18 primary investigations and 1,616 clean experiment runs directly into the web app so filtering and plotting happen instantaneously in the browser.

• 6-Engine Backend & 4-Tier Safety Guardrails: Our backend combines (1) a 12-equation Partial-Gravity PINN + Gaussian Process Regressor (<0.08% error bridging 0g ACME E-FIELD ion-wind data to Lunar/Martian gravity), (2) a Temporal JEPA model forecasting +5s/+10s/+30s flame growth and cabin pressure rise, (3) a <1 ms XGBoost regime classifier, (4) OpenCV soot optical-depth analysis (separating smoke α > 1.8 from lunar dust α < 0.7), (5) a 6D Mahalanobis archive matcher and inverse thickness solver, and (6) hybrid RAG retrieval with Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct. Four guardrail tiers block out-of-range sensor spikes, enforce true thermodynamic slopes, apply hard quench/runaway vetoes, and block fake PSI IDs, passing 32 out of 32 audit checks in 6.79 ms average latency.

IMPORTANT NOTE FOR JUDGES: 3-TIER HYBRID FAILOVER & LIVE GPU AVAILABILITY

Because our trained 6-engine backend (Active Combustion Model) runs on an on-demand cloud T4 GPU server, the live GPU tunnel cannot stay powered on 24/7 after our session ends. To make sure judges never hit a dead page or broken chat, we built a 3-tier failover system into the web app:

• Tier 1 (Active Combustion Model): Connects directly to our live GPU FastAPI server when our Colab session is running.

• Tier 2 (Local Combustion Model): When the cloud GPU is offline, the web app automatically switches to our Local Combustion Model. It calculates exact chamber physics, nearest PSI runs, and clickable charts in the browser first, and feeds that real telemetry packet to Gemini 3.8 Flash so the Model Console stays conversational and grounded in real numbers.

• Tier 3 (Offline Physics Core): If external APIs hit rate limits or run completely offline, the browser's 12-equation physics engine and 1,616-run archive keep every simulation, chart, and comparison working with zero downtime.

Judges can inspect our full model training pipeline, ONNX/XGBoost weights, and the complete 32/32 Certified Audit output anytime in the Google Colab notebook inside our GitHub repository.

REAL-WORLD IMPACT (SPACE & EARTH)

We validated FLARE across 10 spaceflight benchmarks, including the ISS Destiny Lab, Artemis Lunar Habitat and Rover, Mars Base, xEMU Spacesuit Loop, Apollo 1, Apollo 13, Mir 1997, and Cygnus Saffire-III, and structured our data schema for NASA's upcoming LUCI and FM2 lunar payloads. On Earth, the same models help contain thermal runaway in EV lithium-ion battery packs, qualify materials for high-oxygen hyperbaric medical chambers and submarines, design low-emission industrial burners, and prevent dust false alarms in wildfire and cleanroom smoke detectors.

SUPER INTELLIGENCE (SI) & DATA ATTRIBUTION NOTE

Google Gemini was used during development for frontend and backend code scaffolding, TypeScript/UI debugging, and initial architectural brainstorming. All combustion physics equations, flame-spread predictions, and experimental benchmarks are governed by deterministic fluid mechanics and verified NASA Physical Science Informatics (PSI) records (non-SI). FLARE is an independent student project created by Team The Straw Hats for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge and is not affiliated with or endorsed by NASA.
